_comment: What this list is: permission-prompt reduction for the commands this project runs
constantly, narrowed to the actual invocations. What it is NOT: a sandbox or a
security boundary. Rules are prefix-matched, and twice now that has quietly restored
an outward action the list meant to exclude: `Bash(uv run *)` and `Bash(python3 *)`
matched `uv run git push` and any Python subprocess (round 1), then `Bash(scripts/*)`
matched finish-item.sh --delete-remote, which pushes a branch deletion (round 2).
So: no interpreter wildcards, no directory wildcards over scripts/ or
listed one at a time by name. finish-item.sh is deliberately absent -- a prefix rule
cannot tell it apart from its --delete-remote form, so it prompts every run, which is
once per merge. git push, gh pr create and gh pr merge are absent for the same reason.
Nothing here can stop a cooperating agent from reaching the network, but the operator
is now actually the boundary on outward actions rather than nominally one. Add exact
commands as they come up; never widen a prefix back out to a directory or interpreter.
